learning_outcomes.text: Students can describe the position and orientation of industrial robots using Euler angles, Euler parameters, quaternions, and Denavit-Hartenberg parameters.
They understand how Newton-Euler equations can be used in the simulation of robots.
They are able to perform the described calculations analytically or with the help of suitable simulation software.
They can also design motion profiles for drives for various movement types such as Point-to-Point, synchronous Point-to-Point, and Continuous Path movements.
They can then implement these typical movement types programmatically with the training cells at the end of the course.
Students are able to create programmatic solutions for robot applications, including the integration of camera systems.

syllabus_topics: Familiarization with and handling of various robot coordinate systems and robot movements and related practical problems
Integration of additional sensors such as cameras
Kinematics of robot systems: Degrees of freedom of mechanisms
Description of position and orientation of bodies in space: Rotation matrices, Euler angles, Euler parameters, Homogeneous Coordinates/Denavit-Hartenberg parameters
Movement methods: PTP, synchronous PTP, CP
Application of simulation software to perform the above calculations
Calculations using simulation software for robot kinematics
Compulsory tasks on the robot for essential chapters in robot programming

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (Kl/45) or oral exam (MP/20) in Robot Kinematics
Graded practical work in Robot Programming
Ungraded successful completion of the Robot Laboratory (exercises on the robot cell and Matlab exercises)

assessment_rules: The examination form will be announced at the beginning of the semester. The overall assessment includes a graded written exam (Kl/45) or an oral exam (MP/20) in Robot Kinematics, a graded practical work in Robot Programming, and the ungraded successful completion of the Robot Laboratory (exercises on the robot cell and Matlab exercises).
